name: Exodus
description: Exodus - Deliverance from Egypt and covenant at Sinai
intro: Exodus narrates Israel's deliverance from slavery in Egypt and the establishment of the covenant at Sinai. This foundational act of redemption becomes the pattern for understanding God's saving work throughout Scripture, pointing forward to the greater exodus accomplished in Christ.

themes.title: Redemption and deliverance
themes.body: God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt establishes the paradigm for all biblical salvation: grace precedes law, redemption before obedience. The Passover and Red Sea crossing reveal God as the one who saves by blood and power.

themes.title: The name and glory of God
themes.body: God reveals himself by name as YHWH, "I AM WHO I AM," the covenant-keeping God of promise. His glory fills the tabernacle, making his presence visible and dwelling among his people.

themes.title: Covenant and law
themes.body: The Sinai covenant establishes Israel as God's treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The Ten Commandments and the Book of the Covenant define covenant life under God's rule.

themes.title: The tabernacle
themes.body: Nearly half of Exodus details the tabernacle's design and construction. This portable sanctuary enables God to dwell among his people, foreshadowing the incarnation and the ultimate temple of Christ's body.

themes.title: Mediation and intercession
themes.body: Moses stands between God and the people as mediator, foreshadowing the greater mediator to come. His intercession after the golden calf incident reveals the logic of substitutionary atonement.

structure.title: Slavery and Deliverance (1–18)
structure.body: Israel's oppression in Egypt, Moses' call, ten plagues, Passover, Red Sea crossing, and journey to Sinai.

structure.title: Covenant at Sinai (19–24)
structure.body: Theophany at Sinai, Ten Commandments, Book of the Covenant, and covenant ratification.

structure.title: Tabernacle Instructions (25–31)
structure.body: Detailed plans for the tabernacle, priesthood, and worship.

structure.title: Golden Calf and Renewal (32–34)
structure.body: Israel's idolatry, Moses' intercession, covenant renewal, and revelation of God's character.

structure.title: Tabernacle Construction (35–40)
structure.body: The people build the tabernacle according to the divine pattern, and God's glory fills it.

whyRead: Exodus establishes the vocabulary of redemption that echoes through the entire Bible. Understanding the exodus is essential for reading the prophets, the Psalms, and the New Testament's presentation of Jesus as the paschal lamb who accomplishes the true and final exodus.
